A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KORE research despite retitling and reformatting. All 34 pages of v1 and 32 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original knowledge-adaptation and retention experiments on three multimodal models, alongside ablations, covariance analyses and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional baseline and evaluation-metric results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The augmentation pipeline, covariance-based null-space projection, adapter initialization, residual weight adjustment and freezing of A while training B remain unchanged. The knowledge-oriented controls and two-stage terminology reframe the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use EVOKE, KORE-74K, OneVision covariance samples and the same 12 retention benchmarks. The news/entity coverage and diagnostic scenarios are retained; the new OneVision illustration does not establish additional coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds CIA to the LLaVA-v1.5 (7B) adaptation, retention and fine-grained comparisons, increasing the main baseline set from eight to nine. The other comparators remain; changed SEFE scores do not establish a changed baseline procedure.

E3.justification: Section 4 adds HARS and changes the retention aggregation underlying overall Avg from seven capability averages to twelve benchmark scores. For example, KORE's retention aggregate becomes 40.00 instead of 38.22. Listed training settings and evaluation tasks otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The rank/component ablations, covariance reconstruction and sampling analyses, targeted constraints, augmentation comparisons, convergence curves and case studies are retained. Revised score summaries and relocated displays do not introduce new diagnostic experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained dataset statistics are descriptive counts, not experimental uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 substantially revises result reporting through CIA results, pretrained-model adaptation scores and HARS values across the experimental comparisons. SEFE's Table 1 CEM/F1 change from 13.38/16.88 to 16.22/24.12. KORE rank-235 Avg changes from 37.09 to 37.98 through reaggregation, while its CEM/F1 remain 30.65/41.26. Some cross-model aggregate values are also corrected.

T1.justification: v2 introduces the mathematical definition of HARS and its relative-gain transformations in Equation (4). Appendix C mainly reformulates the existing knowledge-preservation arguments rather than adding a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that structured augmentation and knowledge-oriented adapter constraints improve adaptation while preserving prior capabilities across model scales and architectures. The new contribution bullets and controls terminology restate existing contributions, including KORE-74K.

C2.justification: v2 removes the substantive limitations concerning GPT-4o hallucinations, augmentation of individual knowledge units and expensive covariance extraction, and replaces specific misuse concerns with a generic impact statement. It adds an interpretation that shared GPT-4o usage proves augmentation-design benefits rather than mere distillation, and presents the Qwen comparison as justification for HARS.

D1.justification: v2 adds baseline implementation-source citations but removes the project link, planned code/data/weights release information, Replay's LoRA and 10%-of-EVOKE recipe, and explicit 64-per-category OneVision sampling detail. Training hyperparameters, hardware and augmentation prompts remain available and unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 substantially revises the continual-learning positioning into regularization, architecture, rehearsal and prompt-based categories, adding numerous relevant works. New references include CIA, AlphaEdit, PackNet and prompt-based approaches; some earlier projection-method references disappear. These changes exceed bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v2 retitles and reframes the narrative around knowledge-oriented controls, adds explicit contribution bullets, rewrites related-work and results passages, and removes standalone limitations and reproducibility sections. The appendices reorganize augmentation details and case studies and separate prompts into Appendix I.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout. Figure 2 is redesigned, Figures 1, 5 and 7 are revised, and a OneVision sampling diagram is added. Main tables emphasize aggregate metrics while detailed tables move to the appendix; existing case studies and covariance visualizations are retained.

improvement.justification: Adding CIA, correcting some summaries and improving presentation are useful, but v2 loses substantive limitations and reproducibility disclosures. Its new HARS equation also fails to reproduce Table 1: literal substitution gives approximately 7.49 for KORE rank-235 rather than 82.81, requiring unstated percentage scaling of relative gains. These reporting and transparency losses outweigh the limited gains, while the core method and empirical evidence remain intact.
